Week of 26th October: The school office will be closed for the October half-term holiday from Monday 26th to Friday 30th October and will reopen on Monday 2nd November. We hope everyone has a lovely half-term break. Please note that Monday 2nd November is an INSET Day for staff, so the children will return to school on Tuesday 3rd November. For urgent enquiries, please email admin@nmjs.hants.sch.uk or SEND@nmjs.hants.sch.uk. These mailboxes will be checked periodically throughout the break. We hope everyone has a lovely half-term holiday. 🍂
Welcome
We are delighted to welcome you to the website of New Milton Junior School. If you need to contact the school please call 01425 614633 or email admin@nmjs.hants.sch.uk. Many thanks

New Milton Junior School
About Our School
Visions and Values
Visions and Values
Our vision and values
Our vision and values are at the core of everything we do. They underpin our teaching and learning, and provide an environment which prepares our pupils as confident, happy citizens.
Promoting Fundamental British Values
In accordance with The Department for Education we aim to actively promote British values in schools to ensure young people leave school prepared for life in modern Britain. Pupils are encouraged to regard people of all faiths, races and cultures with respect and tolerance and understand that while different people may hold different views about what is ‘right’ and ‘wrong’, all people living in England are subject to its law.

New Milton Junior School
About Our School
Welcome
Welcome to New Milton Junior School!
We are a busy but friendly school, with lots going on. This website aims to give you a taster of the school, as well as providing regular updated information for both parents and pupils.
We hope that you enjoy your visit to our website, and that you find any information you are looking for. Please feel free to leave comments in the Guestbook, or contact the school direct with any queries you may have. Thank you for visiting!
A very warm welcome from the Headteacher and Staff;
Your child is very important to us. We hope we can work together to forge a real partnership between us. We have high expectations and set high standards for your son or daughter. Our positive and active home-school partnership will help your child to make the most of his or her time at New Milton Junior. We hope that this website will answer some of the questions you may have about the school. Please do not feel shy about coming to talk to members of staff, governors or myself.
TOGETHER TOWARDS OUR VERY BEST

pageCache.pageTitle: New Milton Junior School - NMJS Breakfast Club / NMIS Twilight Club
pageCache.text:
New Milton Junior School
Parents & Guardians
NMJS Breakfast Club / NMIS Twilight Club
NMJS Breakfast Club / NMIS Twilight Club
Breakfast Club: Information
Breakfast Club is open from 7.45 am each day, and is located in the Junior School Hall, which can be accessed through the door to the left of the reception. A breakfast of cereal, toast/jam/butter, (when available, pancakes or waffles) plus apple or orange juice is offered each morning until 8:15 am.
Places will be allocated on a first-come first-served basis. Payment is required in advance of your child attending the session. Please pay cash or cheque via the school office. Cheques should be made payable to Hampshire County Council. We also use Scopay as our online payment system and you will be provided with a code for the initial setup.
If your child is unable to attend the club, we will refund the cost of the session booked as long as you notify us before 7:45 am on the day of the booking. To cancel please call or email the junior school.
You will still be charged if a place is booked and you do not cancel the booking.
Breakfast Club Booking Form: Autumn 2026
Breakfast Club: Bookings Available on Scopay
I am very pleased to advise that bookings for the Breakfast Club can be managed Via Scopay. Once logged into Scopay you will see an 'Order Sessions' option under the breakfast club heading.
This will allow you to book or cancel future sessions for the school year. Just click on the day required and select the option 'attending', then ok. This will book a place for your child.
To cancel, select the day and then choose 'no option' which will remove the booking and refund your account.
If the session is full please contact the office and we will do our best to accommodate you.
You will not be able to make bookings or cancellations for the next day and you will still need to contact the office to make amendments if they are within 24 hours of the session.
Please note that the online booking system is for standard bookings only, i.e. those charged at £4.00. This does not include any concession bookings that will still need to be approved via the office.
Payments for the breakfast club can still be made in the same way, either online via Scopay, transfers from Government Schemes, or cash/cheque via the school office. We ask that all sessions be paid for in advance and we will continue to send out reminders for any payments outstanding 1 week in advance, on Fridays.
If you have not registered for Scopay please contact the office and we will send your Scopay registration letter and link code.
We will still accept bookings via the junior school office if you prefer not to use the online facility. Please note that all bookings are on a first-come first-served basis.
If you have any questions please do not hesitate to contact the school office at 01425 614633 or by emailing admin@nmjs.hants.sch.uk
Twilight Club
Twilight is an OFSTED registered (115928) Wrapround Childcare after school club for children who attend both New Milton Infant School and New Milton Junior School. Twilight is open from 3.15 - 6 pm on school days and is located at New Milton Infant School.

Important News re: Guitar
Date: 8th September 2026
Dear parents/carers It is with regret that we inform you that we are currently unable to provide guitar lessons.
Recent changes to teacher availability have meant that Hampshire Music Services are unable to provide us with a teacher.
We know that many pupils look forward to these lessons, and we are sorry for any disappointment this may cause.
We will continue to look for ways to restore guitar teaching as soon as we are able.
I would like to thank you for your patience and understanding during this time.
With kind regards, New Milton Junior School

Parents & Guardians

New Milton Junior School
Curriculum
New Milton Junior School Curriculum
‘Moving together towards our very best’ is at the heart of the curriculum at New Milton Junior School. Our pupils are provided with a vibrant, engaging, knowledge-rich curriculum that equips them with the skills and understanding necessary to be active, responsible citizens in an ever-evolving world.
Six core values drive our broad and balanced curriculum.
To be: respectful, honest, caring, supportive, responsible and to achieve.
We expect success from all of our pupils. Everyone is encouraged to achieve as individuals, in preparation for how they will contribute to society, the economy and the environment.
At New Milton Junior School, learning is at heart of all that we do: our curriculum is highly inclusive and our teaching is adaptive to meet all needs. Where fitting, activities are driven by the personal interests of the pupils and culture of our community, both local and from around the world. They will develop their knowledge and skills throughout the year and will have opportunities to retrieve their understanding at different points to ensure they do not forget what they have learnt.
Find information about our curriculum below.
If you wish to discuss any elements of your child's education, please talk to the class teacher or speak to Mr Geary or Mrs Grinyer.
Parents and carers have the right to withdraw children from all or part of RE / RSE lessons. Please make an appointment via the school office to discuss this.
I would like to celebrate the energy, commitment and enthusiasm for reading that I see across the school on a daily basis be it in class; paired reading between the upper and lower school children; library sessions; a storyteller joining Year 5; and even in my book club!
Over time, our goal is to foster a sense of curiosity where books and the written word can not only lead us places, but spark a further line of enquiry for each and everyone of us. It has been wonderful to see all of our classes regularly hitting their ‘target read’ every week, resulting in them having a brand new book of their choosing delivered weekly to their class bookshelf.
Reading events in the hall have been a lot of fun where children have enjoyed reading comics and Mindfulness Activity cards with partners, listening to stories on SORA or even ‘reading’ a film (subtitles and no sound … a whole new experience!).
Thank you so much for encouraging your child to read to you at home (particularly when days are so busy) as it really does make a significant difference to the progress that they make.
During this term, we are looking forward to further reading events, World Book Day (5th March .. more information to follow) and even another trip to Waterstones for some children.
Thank you again for your support.

New Milton Junior School
Pupil Premium
Pupil Premium
What is Pupil Premium?
The Government believes that the Pupil Premium, which is additional to main school funding, is the best way to address the current underlying inequalities between children eligible for free school meals (FSM) and their wealthier peers by ensuring that funding to tackle disadvantage reaches the pupils who need it most. It is for schools to decide how the Pupil Premium, allocated to schools per FSM pupil, is spent, since they are best placed to assess what additional provision should be made for the individual pupils within their responsibility. Schools are free to spend the Pupil Premium as they see fit. However, they will be held accountable for how they have used the additional funding to support pupils from low-income families. New measures are included in the performance tables that will capture the achievement of those deprived pupils covered by the Pupil Premium.
The Pupil Premium is allocated to children from low-income families who are currently known to be eligible for FSM and children who have been looked after continuously for more than six months. The level of the premium in 2025/26 is £1515 per pupil for pupils eligible for free school meals (FSM) and for pupils in care who have been continuously looked after for six months.
The Pupil Premium grant for the financial year 2025 to 2026 will include pupils recorded in the October 2024 school census who had recorded a period of FSM eligibility since (and including) Jan 2019, as well as those first recorded as eligible in October 2024. At our school, pupil premium allocation is spent either by providing academic support to boost attainment or as a means by which pupils’ learning or experiences in education may be enriched.
